To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

perception of dissonant and consonant chords is accompanied by changes in brain activity in musicians and non-musician, but the patterns of asymmetrical activity in musicians and in non-musician differ.
perception of consonant chords was accompanied by greater theta activity in musicians, while dissonant chords induced greater amplitude of P100 and N200 components.

perception of dissonant and consonant chords in musicians is accompanied by more efficient processing, as evidenced by increased amplitude of early ERP components and less emotional reaction, as indicated by lower theta activation over right anterior regions.
